# How the contacts list is arranged

Which second-level group each contact is in, in what order, and which groups one person has folded away.
The first level is two locked top groups, Human and Agent, DECLARED by the product rather than stored; under
Agent the default second-level groups are by role — secretary, inspector, supervisor, worker, other and
retired — and under Human there is one. Criteria M119 to M121.

SO THESE ROWS ARE ONLY WHAT SOMEBODY CHANGED. A group they made, a default one they renamed or moved, a
contact they moved, an order they set by hand, or a group they folded. An archive with none of these rows is
not an archive of a product with no groups: it is one where nobody has changed the arrangement the product
declares.

AN ARRANGEMENT BELONGS TO A PERSON AND TO THE INSTALLATION, not to a project — which group an agent belongs
in is a fact about the agent, and the registries these arrange are in every project on this machine. So a
project-scoped archive carries none of these, and says so in its notes.

THIS IS ONE PROJECT'S ARCHIVE, so it carries no `contact_groups` rows AT ALL.
A group somebody put their contacts in arranges the two registries, and a person and a durable agent are the same in every project on this machine, so the arrangement belongs to no single one of them, so there is no project whose archive these would be. The database
this was taken from holds 2 of them and they are in NO project's archive; the whole-installation
export is the one that carries them.

SO THIS PAGE IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THERE IS NOTHING TO FIND. It is evidence that you are holding the
wrong archive to find out.

THIS IS ONE PROJECT'S ARCHIVE, so it carries no `contact_placements` rows AT ALL.
Which group a contact was moved into is a fact about that contact, and a person and a durable agent are the same in every project on this machine, so the placement belongs to no single one of them, so there is no project whose archive these would be. The database
this was taken from holds 2 of them and they are in NO project's archive; the whole-installation
export is the one that carries them.

SO THIS PAGE IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THERE IS NOTHING TO FIND. It is evidence that you are holding the
wrong archive to find out.

THIS IS ONE PROJECT'S ARCHIVE, so it carries no `contact_group_collapses` rows AT ALL.
Whether one person has folded a contact group away is a behaviour preference of theirs about the two registries, and those registries are the same in every project on this machine, so the fold belongs to no single one of them, so there is no project whose archive these would be. The database
this was taken from holds 2 of them and they are in NO project's archive; the whole-installation
export is the one that carries them.

SO THIS PAGE IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THERE IS NOTHING TO FIND. It is evidence that you are holding the
wrong archive to find out.
